title: Developer tools: the command line, Git and debugging
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Use a programmer's everyday tools well: the Unix shell and its core commands, files, permissions and processes, pipes and text processing, shell scripts, Git (commits, branches, merging, rebasing, remotes and pull requests), debuggers, logging and profiling, packages and virtual environments, make, and reading documentation.
primary_reading: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT, free)

weeks.1: The shell: navigating and managing files
weeks.3: Pipes, redirection and text tools: grep, sort, uniq and cut
weeks.9: Debugging with a debugger and with logging
weeks.12: Editors, documentation and automation with make

blocks.deliverable: Complete a file-management exercise using only the shell.
Write a script that summarizes a log file.
Create a repository with two branches and merge them.
Week 7 midterm; resolve a merge conflict and open a pull request.
Find a bug with breakpoints and profile a slow function.
Set up a reproducible project with a virtual environment and a Makefile.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Toolsmith project: build a small Python command-line tool in a Git repository with branches and pull requests, a virtual environment and pinned dependencies, a shell script and a Makefile for common tasks, a README, and a written walkthrough of debugging one real bug.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
